claim: New ADRs have a canonical date-prefixed namespace.
limitations: Existing historical numeric ADRs are retained by design.

claim: Focused contracts are documented in the generated inventory and architecture references.
limitations: Generated text is not a substitute for implementation tests.

claim: Generated references are reproducible from typed runtime sources.
limitations: External documentation mirrors are not claimed.

claim: Requirement status and evidence are generated from the append-only ledger.
limitations: Status remains implemented-unverified until broader operational proof exists.

claim: Documentation authority checks detect stale promises and out-of-date generated references.
limitations: The check cannot judge undocumented external promises.

claim: Editor and agent rule documents have a bounded, provider-neutral import/export contract.
limitations: No separately deployed editor transport or live editor SDK integration is claimed.

claim: The operator control-plane snapshot is assembled from all required providers, exposed through an authenticated HTTP facade, and fails closed on incomplete or invalid data.
limitations: Legacy HTTP server route wiring and live runtime provider composition remain separate integration obligations.

claim: The production HTTP handler serves an authenticated, provider-backed control-plane snapshot when explicitly composed and returns a bounded unavailable response when composition is absent or fails.
limitations: The default application graph does not yet populate all fourteen section providers from every live subsystem; absence remains intentionally fail-closed.

claim: The composition root preserves an explicitly supplied complete control-plane provider service and the production HTTP handler consumes that same service boundary.
limitations: The default application graph does not yet populate all fourteen section providers from every live subsystem; absence remains intentionally fail-closed.

claim: The default composition exposes bounded real records for composed control-plane owners and explicit unavailable-state records for unsupported sections; injected provider failures remain fail-closed through the authenticated HTTP route.
limitations: Plans, approvals, context, memory explanations, training, selfmod, updates, and startup authorities still require dedicated owning read ports; their unavailability is explicit rather than inferred.

claim: The default application graph serves the provider-backed control-plane snapshot through the production authenticated HTTP handler, with real health data and explicit unavailable-state records for uncomposed sections.
limitations: Plans, approvals, context, memory explanations, training, selfmod, updates, and startup authorities still require dedicated owning read ports; their unavailability is explicit rather than inferred.

claim: The default control-plane graph reads bounded task plans and approval/action states from their durable owners, redacts approval payloads, and preserves explicit unavailable states for sections without owning read ports.
limitations: Context, memory explanations, training, selfmod, updates, and startup authorities still require dedicated owning read ports; their unavailability is explicit rather than inferred.

claim: The default control-plane graph exposes bounded last-good context metadata and redacted update status alongside durable plans and approvals, without leaking update paths or confirmation nonces.
limitations: Memory explanations, training, selfmod, and startup authorities still require dedicated owning read ports; their unavailability is explicit rather than inferred.

claim: The default control-plane graph adds bounded selfmod run summaries and startup-authority experiment counts from their owning services without exposing commands, output, or environment data.
limitations: Memory explanations and training still require dedicated owning read ports; their unavailability is explicit rather than inferred.

claim: The default control-plane graph reports published training-provider health when a training backend is composed and otherwise preserves an explicit unavailable state.
limitations: Memory explanations still require a dedicated owning read port; training is unavailable when no attended backend is configured.

claim: The default control-plane graph exposes the typed memory policy matrix as bounded explanations without exposing memory content, identifiers, or recall results.
limitations: The projection explains policy and retention rules; per-item recall provenance remains available only through the owning recall/session surfaces.

claim: The native MCP composition exposes negotiated durable task get, update, and cancellation dispatch through the application job service while preserving bounded protocol errors and redacted task views.
limitations: Separately packaged provider deployment and external MCP interoperability acceptance remain unverified; this record does not promote the API-003 checkbox.

claim: The packaged native MCP entrypoint fails closed and reports a bounded refusal before configuration when the mandatory unsafe-lab safety gate rejects the host.
limitations: A successful live packaged-provider exchange still requires a disposable non-elevated host; separately deployed external interoperability remains unverified.

claim: The architecture ratchet rejects reintroduced retired package paths while permitting only the exact reviewed Ollama compatibility shim during caller migration.
limitations: The full ARCH-010 acceptance requirement remains formally unverified; this record covers the retired-path ratchet slice only.

claim: The typed ownership catalog is wired into generated architecture authority artifacts with deterministic layer-level package, state, port, provider, schema, and lifecycle records.
limitations: Resource-level production inventory and the formal ARCH-012 requirement remain unverified; this record covers the generated layer-level projection.

claim: The explicit runtime composition root exposes a protocol application facade whose client schema is bound to the same generated tool catalog and canonical snapshot-plus-events stream contract.
limitations: The inert runtime container does not create live session streams or publish an external SDK package; transport authentication and session-owned stream lifecycle remain host concerns.

claim: The live application graph publishes a redacted provider-health projection for the administrator operations status surface and fails closed to explicit unhealthy state when a typed health probe raises.
limitations: No concrete training/update backend or external deployment receipt is added; provider lifecycle and formal checklist acceptance remain unverified.

claim: The live provider registry and application graph expose scoped cooperative cancellation alongside redacted health for published specialized providers.
limitations: No concrete training/update backend or external deployment receipt is added; provider lifecycle and formal checklist acceptance remain unverified.

claim: The composed subprocess provider publishes bounded stdout and stderr output incrementally through the durable monotonic job-output stream before terminal completion.
limitations: This slice does not claim a full deployment matrix, cross-process provider-handle reconstruction, or formal checklist promotion.

claim: Composed process output uses durable monotonic watermarks with bounded previews and durable spill references while output is live and after restart.
limitations: Reader threads are process-local; restart recovery continues to use durable registry reconciliation and does not silently resume orphan processes.

claim: Durable restart reconciliation has a real subprocess rehearsal: a reopened SQLite registry cleans the persisted process identity through the typed supervisor and records interrupted state only after a complete receipt.
limitations: A full deployment matrix and silent-resume behavior remain outside this slice; orphan work is intentionally not resumed automatically.

claim: The production application graph can publish injected attended training and update providers alongside embedding, expose typed health, propagate cooperative cancellation, and close all published providers through the application lifecycle boundary.
limitations: Default training/update backends remain absent by policy; external deployment receipts and formal architecture acceptance remain unverified.

claim: The live application graph exposes typed provider-neutral training and update operation entrypoints that resolve scoped providers, fail closed when a lane is absent or lacks the capability, and return normalized deployment or activation evidence.
limitations: Default training/update backends remain absent by policy; external deployment receipts, full-system regression, and formal architecture acceptance remain unverified.
